title: Prebuilt Database Providers and Maturity
readerIntent: Select a database adapter using truthful implementation and release evidence.
summary: A module slot or deterministic contract is not production qualification; the selected provider must prove live connectivity, isolation, transactions, failure, recovery, and performance for the target topology.

sections.heading: MongoDB
paragraphs: MongoDB is the implemented primary adapter for connection, schema, model, query, index, middleware, and transaction mapping. Transactions require a replica set or sharded cluster; a standalone local server is not transaction-qualified. Production use still requires live release qualification.

sections.heading: Cassandra and Elastic database adapters
paragraphs: Their repository modules are extension evidence, not permission to claim feature parity or production readiness. Confirm actual connection, model, query, schema, transaction, tenant-isolation, and lifecycle implementations before selection.

sections.heading: Selection criteria
items: Consistency, availability, recovery, and migration requirements.
Supported versions, security controls, operational skills, and cost.
Live contract, load, outage, reconnect, backup, restore, and upgrade evidence.

sections.heading: Provider maturity levels
items: A module placeholder proves only intended extension structure.
A deterministic mock or contract test proves interface shape, not live engine behavior.
A live local test proves basic connectivity and operations for one version and topology.
Release qualification proves supported versions, security, isolation, failure, recovery, performance, and operations.
Production approval remains deployment-specific and time-bounded.

sections.heading: MongoDB operating fit
paragraphs: MongoDB is the current primary implemented persistence path and is appropriate when document-oriented models, indexes, queries, and supported transactions match the product. Nodics still owns schema composition, tenant resolution, middleware, and normalized errors.
Replica-set transaction requirements, index rollout, connection pools, backup, restore, sharding, upgrade, and failure behavior must be qualified for the target deployment.

sections.heading: Cassandra assessment
paragraphs: Cassandra favors query-driven denormalized modeling, partition-key design, horizontal scale, and eventual-consistency choices. A generic document-schema mapping cannot be assumed to provide equivalent queries or transactions.
Before selection, verify actual handler completeness, relationship strategy, migrations, tenant partitioning, batch semantics, repair, backup, restore, topology change, and operational expertise.

sections.heading: Elastic database assessment
paragraphs: Elasticsearch is normally a search projection rather than the authoritative transactional database. An elastic database adapter must not be confused with the separate search-provider capability.
Using it for authoritative persistence requires explicit evidence for consistency, update conflicts, schema mapping, retention, recovery, access control, and every required business operation.

sections.heading: Decision example
paragraphs: A Profile and commerce deployment requiring governed CRUD, relationships, indexes, and transactional updates may select the qualified MongoDB adapter. Product discovery can still use Elasticsearch through Search as a derived index.
The decision records why the provider fits, which capabilities are unsupported, how tenants are placed, and which tests and runbooks qualify the selected versions.

sections.heading: Evidence before production
items: Provider contract suite against a real instance.
Tenant and module isolation under concurrency.
Representative CRUD, query, relationship, index, and transaction workloads.
Credential rotation, encryption, network restriction, and audit.
Startup outage, mid-operation failure, retry, reconnect, failover, and shutdown.
Backup restore, migration rollback, version upgrade, load, soak, and capacity evidence.
